_readme: Phenomenon-first prompt lines for the Unit 1 dashboard mode header band. Each prompt asks students to notice or predict something observable — it must not name the underlying science concept. Edit this file to change prompts; do not hardcode prompt text in panel components.

solar.prompt: Watch this line for the next five minutes. What would make it jump?
solar.alt: A live measurement from a satellite 1.5 million km from Earth is updating on this screen right now.

solar-system.prompt: Pick two planets. Which one will move farther across this view in one month?
solar-system.alt: Every dot here is in motion right now, even though it looks still from one date to the next.

borrelly.prompt: Drag the slider toward the Sun. What do you predict happens to this object as it gets closer?
borrelly.alt: This icy traveler swings from the outer solar system to inside Earth's orbit and back, over and over.

exoplanet.prompt: If you could only send one instrument to this world, what would you want to measure first?
exoplanet.alt: Every value on this card came from a real telescope measurement or survey, not a guess.

host-star.prompt: Two stars can be the same temperature and look totally different sizes. How could that be?
host-star.alt: This star anchors an entire planetary system — everything in it depends on this one object.

observing.prompt: Name one thing in the sky tonight that you could point to and say 'that is really there, right now.'
observing.alt: Step outside tonight and some of these targets will be exactly where this screen says.
